title: 5 Best Shampoos for Curly Hair Recommended by Dermatologists
summary: Struggling with dry, frizzy curls? Learn the biophysics of curly hair, top shampoo picks, and an expert 5-step haircare routine for healthy coils.
body_text: Why Standard Shampoo Fail Difference between Traditional & Curly Hair Shampoos Best Shampoos for Curly Hair Haircare Routine for Curly Hair FAQs Do you often find managing your curly hair difficult? Curls are stunning, bouncy, and undeniably full of character; but let’s be honest, they can also be a total nightmare to manage. From mystery knots that seem to appear out of thin air to ends that are perpetually thirsty no matter how much product you dump on them, caring for curly hair often feels like solving a daily riddle. As you have special hair, they definitely need special treatment. In this article, we’ll understand the mechanism of your hair, and find out some of the best shampoo for curly hair, recommended by dermatologists. Biophysical Reality of Curly Hair & Why Standard Shampoos Fail From a trichological perspective, hair is composed of a keratin core protected by overlapping cuticle scales, glued together by the cell membrane complex (CMC). In straight hair, the hair follicle is cylindrical, allowing natural sebum (a mixture of squalene, wax esters, and triglycerides) to travel easily down the smooth fiber. Curly hair grows from asymmetrical, curved follicles, producing an oval cross-section characterized by twists along the shaft. These continuous curves create two major physiological vulnerabilities: Sebic Obstruction: Scalp lipids cannot easily navigate the twists and turns of a spiral, leaving the mid-lengths and ends inherently lipid-deficient. Exposed Cuticle Margins: The outer cuticle scales lift slightly along the outer apex of each curve or kink, creating points of high mechanical stress and elevated porosity. Conventional shampoos are designed around strong anionic surfactants (such as sodium lauryl sulfate) formulated to aggressively emulsify and strip lipids from oily, straight hair shafts. When applied to curly hair, these harsh cleansers strip away the vital hydrophobic monolayer, specifically 18-methyl eicosanoic acid (18-MEA) that protects the cuticle layer. Stripping 18-MEA leaves the hair hydrophilic, causing the fiber to swell in humid conditions and resulting in severe frizz, static, and shaft fracturing. How Shampoos Formulated for Curly Hair Differ Chemically Shampoos formulated specifically for curly hair prioritize lipid preservation and charge neutralization over aggressive surface degreasing. The key formulation differences are governed by three primary chemical mechanisms: 1. Surfactant Mildness & Micellar Charge Instead of harsh sulfates, curly hair shampoos rely on mild anionic cleansers (like sodium cocoyl isethionate), non-ionic surfactants, or amphoteric surfactants (such as cocamidopropyl betaine). These milder molecules form gentler micelles that remove superficial dirt and excess sebum without stripping the structural lipids within the cell membrane complex. 2. Neutralization of Electrostatic Repulsion Hair fibers naturally carry a net negative electrical charge, which is amplified when dirt and sebum are washed away. In curly hair, mutual repulsion between negatively charged strands causes individual fibers to push away from each other, breaking up curl clusters and creating frizz. Curly hair shampoos incorporate cationic conditioning agents (such as polyquaterniums or guar hydroxypropyltrimonium chloride) that deposit onto the shaft during washing to neutralize this charge, reducing friction and restoring curl alignment. 3. Lipid Replenishment & Cuticle Sealing To offset the inherent structural dryer state of curly hair, these specialized shampoos include bio-identical lipids, fatty alcohols, and lightweight plant oils. During the wash cycle, these lipophilic molecules bind to areas where 18-MEA has been depleted, restoring a hydrophobic barrier over exposed cuticles and preventing excessive water absorption into the inner cortex. Top 5 Shampoos for Curly Hair There are a variety of curly hair products available in the market, finding the right shampoo needs the understanding of key ingredients, and their specific benefits. To ease your search, here are 5 best shampoos for curly hair, suggested by dermatologists: Products Key Ingredients Benefits Beauty Garage Pure African Shea Butter Retention Treatment Wavy Curl Shampoo Pure African Shea Butter (Butyrospermum Parkii Oil), Proteins and Amino Acids, Cocamidopropyl Betaine & Sodium Coceth Sulfate, Chamomile Extract (Anthemis Nobilis Flower Extract),Dimethicone & Citric Acid Deeply moisturizes and defines waves and curls. Cleanses gently without stripping natural oils, reducing frizz. Strengthens hair fibers with proteins and amino acids. Enhances natural wave/curl patterns and promotes elasticity. Suitable for regular use on wavy and curly hair types. The Curl Co Cleanse & Hydrate Curl Shampoo Plantcol, Shea Butter, Argan Oil, Sunflohair, Proquinoa HQ Gently cleanses the scalp and hair while removing buildup. Retains hydration and nourishes dry curls. Adds shine, softness, and smoothness without weighing hair down. Supports scalp health and freshness. Strengthens and restores strands. Curl Up Curl Moisturising Shampoo Argan Oil, Chia Seed Extract & Flax Seed Extract, Coconut-Based Surfactants, Aloe Vera Extract, Panthenol & Glycerin, Hydrolyzed Wheat Protein & Jojoba Oil Gently cleanses without drying or stripping natural oils. Enhances curl definition, shine, and elasticity. Reduces frizz and tames flyaways. Strengthens and softens hair strands from within. Free from sulfates, parabens, and silicones. Giovanni Curl Habit Curl Defining Shampoo Coconut Oil (Cocos Nucifera Oil), Shea Butter (Butyrospermum Parkii Butter), Avocado Oil (Persea Gratissima Oil), Olive Fruit Oil (Olea Europaea) & Jojoba Oil (Simmondsia Chinensis), Rosemary, Lemongrass & Lavender Extracts Gently cleanses all curl types with a light lather. Enhances natural curl definition and bounce. Leaves curls soft, fresh, and naturally manageable. Improves the texture of dry strands without adding heaviness. Silicone-free and color-safe formula. Manetain Moisturising Shampoo Baobab Protein, Seaweed Extract & Marshmallow Extract, Aloe Vera Leaf Extract & D-Panthenol, Alpha Olefin Sulphonate & Cocamidopropyl Betaine, Cetrimonium Chloride & Orange Essential Oil Gently cleanses the scalp and hair, removing impurities. Moisturizes dry, frizzy, and textured hair without stripping. Supports softer curls/waves and improves bounce. Enhances shine and overall manageability. Reduces frizz while cleansing. 1. Beauty Garage Pure African Shea Butter Retention Treatment Shampoo Designed as a heavy-duty moisture and repair treatment, this shampoo pairs rich plant lipids with structural proteins to revive compromised, high-porosity curls. It cleanses while creating a protective layer over vulnerable cuticles, making it ideal for thick or damaged textures that suffer from severe dry-weather breakage and loss of elasticity. Rich Moisture Retention: Enriched with pure African shea butter (Butyrospermum Parkii Oil), it delivers deep hydration to lipid-starved lengths and ends, helping to prevent moisture loss. Protein & Amino Acid Fortification: The inclusion of proteins and amino acids helps patch weak structural points along the curved hair shaft, strengthening hair fibers and restoring elasticity. Frizz & Texture Management: By gently cleansing while conditioning, it smooths the cuticle layer, reducing frizz and enhancing wave and curl definition. Who Should Avoid: It contains Sodium Coceth Sulfate (a modified sulfate cleanser) and Dimethicone (a non-water-soluble silicone), making it unsuitable for those avoiding sulfates and silicones. 2. The Curl Co Cleanse & Hydrate Curl Shampoo Formulated as a lightweight daily-care cleanser, this shampoo strikes a balance between clearing away scalp impurities and restoring natural movement. It uses proprietary botanical complexes and lightweight oils to revive limp curls, focusing on weightless bounce and manageable shine without leaving heavy residues behind. Balanced Hydration & Cleansing: Formulated to effectively clear away product buildup and daily impurities from the scalp without leaving curls dry, rough, or stripped. Nutrient-Dense Formulation: Uses a blend of botanical extracts (Sunflohair, Plantcol, Proquinoa HQ) along with Shea Butter and Argan Oil to deeply nourish strands and restore softness. Lightweight Bounce: Provides smoothness and shine while keeping curls feeling weightless, refreshed, and ready for leave-in conditioners. Who Should Avoid: Ingredients like Proquinoa HQ and specialized plant proteins can cause protein-sensitive curls to feel stiff, straw-like, or brittle if used too frequently. 3. Curl Up Curl Moisturising Shampoo Built specifically for low-to-medium porosity curls prone to frizz, this sulfate-free formula relies on natural plant mucilage and mild coconut cleansers. It prioritizes surface smoothing and moisture retention by creating a protective, moisture-locking film around each strand during the wash cycle. Gentle, Sulfate-Free Cleansing: Uses mild, coconut-based surfactants that cleanse the scalp while preserving the hair’s natural protective 18-MEA lipid layer. Dual Seed-Extract Support: Features Chia Seed and Flax Seed extracts, which work together to boost thickness, improve elasticity, and form a gel-like film over strands to lock in curl definition and tame flyaways. Deep Conditioning: Infused with Argan Oil, Jojoba Oil , Hydrolyzed Wheat Protein, Aloe Vera, and Panthenol to nourish dry curls and reduce static. Who Should Avoid: It contains Hydrolyzed Wheat Protein; those with severe contact sensitivities to wheat-derived ingredients should perform a patch test first. 4. Giovanni Curl Habit Curl Defining Shampoo Rooted in botanical science, this formula focuses on restoring soft texture and shine through a multi-oil botanical blend rather than synthetic smoothing agents. It acts as an ultra-gentle, silicone-free wash that softens stiff strands and enlivens the scalp with invigorating plant essences. Botanical Oil Blend: Combines Coconut, Avocado , Olive, and Jojoba oils to restore lipids along exposed cuticles, softening coarse, dry strands. Silicone-Free Definition: Creates a light, gentle lather that cleanses without heavy silicones or harsh drying agents, keeping color-treated hair vibrant and soft. Aromatic Scalp Refresher: Contains botanical extracts like Rosemary, Lemongrass, and Lavender to refresh the scalp and support healthy hair growth. Who Should Avoid: The natural essential oil extracts (Lemongrass, Lavender, Rosemary) give a pleasant scent but can cause contact irritation on hypersensitive or eczema-prone scalps. 5. Manetain Moisturising Shampoo Engineered to combat mechanical friction and wet-detangling damage, this formula combines plant-derived proteins, high-slip botanicals, and charge-neutralizing agents. It provides superior slip during washing, making it easier to manage tightly coiled, tangle-prone patterns without causing fiber damage. Slippery Detangling & Film Forming: Infused with Marshmallow Extract and Seaweed Extract, which provide natural slip and hydration to help detangle textured hair during washing. Structural Repair: Utilizes Baobab Protein and D-Panthenol to penetrate the hair shaft, repairing micro-cracks and boosting elasticity to reduce breakage. Frizz Neutralization: Contains Cetrimonium Chloride (a cationic conditioning agent) that neutralizes negative static charge on the hair surface, helping curl clusters align smoothly. Who Should Avoid: It contains Orange Essential Oil, which may irritate individuals with allergic contact dermatitis or inflamed scalps. Doctor’s Suggested Haircare Routine for Curly Hair A dermatologist-approved routine for curly hair focuses on scalp health, barrier preservation, and moisture retention. Because the curvature of curly hair makes it naturally prone to friction, dryness, and breakage, a clinical approach emphasizes gentle cleansing and protection over mechanical force. Step 1: Pre-Wash Detangling & Scalp Prep Technique: Never brush or detangle dry hair. Apply a coat of lightweight hair oil or a wet detangling spray to provide slip, then use your fingers or a wide-tooth comb starting at the ends and working upward toward the scalp. Dermatologist Reason: Wet or lubricated hair is much more pliable; dry brushing causes high tensile stress that fractures the hair shaft along curved weak points. Step 2: Gentle Cleansing (1–2 Times Weekly) Technique: Apply a sulfate-free, moisturizing shampoo directly to the scalp only. Gently massage the scalp with finger pads (not nails) to clear sebum and debris. Allow the lather to rinse down through the mid-lengths without aggressive scrubbing. Dermatologist Reason: Heavy sulfates strip away the protective hydrophobic 18-MEA layer, leaving hair prone to environmental damage and frizz. Note on Scalp Care: If you suffer from dandruff or seborrheic dermatitis, apply targeted anti-dandruff treatments only to the scalp for 2–10 minutes, followed by a moisturizing wash on the hair lengths to prevent extreme drying. Step 3: Deep Conditioning & Cuticle Sealing Technique: Apply a generous amount of a thick conditioner or deep-conditioning mask containing fatty alcohols (e.g., cetyl or stearyl alcohol), ceramides, or plant oils. Focus heavily on mid-lengths to ends. Leave it on for 5–10 minutes before rinsing with lukewarm or cool water. Dermatologist Reason: Fatty alcohols and ceramides help smooth the raised cuticles along the curves, locking moisture into the cortex and minimizing friction between neighboring strands. Step 4: Moisture Locking (The LOC/LCO Method) While hair is still soaking wet, layer products from thinnest to thickest consistency to seal in hydration: L - Liquid/Leave-in Conditioner: Replenishes base hydration. O/C - Oil or Cream: Smooths the cuticle and defines natural curl clusters. Gel/Styler (Optional): Forms a protective temporary film cast around curl clumps to shield them from atmospheric humidity and reduce frizz as they dry. Step 5: Low-Friction Drying Technique: Avoid rough, traditional terrycloth cotton towels. Gently squeeze out excess water using a microfiber towel or a soft cotton t-shirt. Air-dry, or use a blow dryer on a low heat setting with a diffuser attachment to distribute air evenly. Dermatologist Reason: Heat over 350°F (175°C) and the abrasive texture of heavy towels break the structural hydrogen bonds in hair, permanently degrading curl elasticity and definition. Overnight & Maintenance Protection Silk/Satin Sleep Gear: Use a silk or satin pillowcase, or wear a satin bonnet/scarf. Unlike cotton, silk does not absorb moisture from the hair fiber or create mechanical friction while you sleep. Low-Tension Hairstyles: If tying hair up, use a loose pineapple style or soft scrunchies. Avoid excessively tight ponytails or tight braids to reduce the risk of traction alopecia (hair loss caused by strain on the roots). Final Thought: Making Right Choices for Your Curly Hair Finding the right hair care routine for curly hair is a personal journey grounded in understanding your unique strand texture, porosity, and scalp needs. By prioritizing sulfate-free cleansers, nutrient-dense conditioners, and low-friction styling methods, you can protect your hair’s natural moisture barrier and enhance curl definition without causing unnecessary breakage. Utilizing products formulated with hydrating lipids, botanical oils, and mild surfactants helps keep your curls healthy, resilient, and manageable every day. However, because scalp conditions and individual hair sensitivities vary widely, it is always best to consult a dermatologist or qualified trichologist before introducing new products or active treatments into your routine. A board-certified expert can evaluate your scalp health, identify potential allergens or underlying issues like seborrheic dermatitis, and provide personalized recommendations tailored specifically to your hair's unique needs.

title: 7 Claude Cowork Limitations That Break Enterprise AI Workflows
summary: Claude Cowork has 7 critical gaps for regulated enterprises: no audit logs, no RBAC, no on-prem, and Anthropic's own docs advise against compliance workloads.
body_text: Summary Claude Cowork lacks critical enterprise features like audit logs, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and on-premise deployment, which are non-negotiable for regulated industries. Anthropic's own documentation explicitly warns against using Claude Cowork for regulated workloads, posing a significant compliance and legal liability for enterprises. The unpredictable, consumption-based pricing of LLM tools creates a budgeting nightmare for CFOs; a deterministic approach can be 15-60x more cost-effective at scale. Regulated enterprises need a purpose-built AI workflow platform with immutable audit logs, team governance, and deployment flexibility like Jinba Flow . There's no denying the buzz around Claude Cowork. As one of the most capable AI assistants on the market, it's genuinely impressive for individual productivity — summarizing documents, drafting emails, brainstorming strategies. But for leaders in banking, insurance, legal, and healthcare, that excitement tends to hit a hard wall the moment you ask a simple question: "Is this auditable?" The answer, too often, is no. As enterprise practitioners have noted in the wild, "most tools really do focus on generic sales insights and skip the compliance side." In a regulated environment, the output can't just be a neat summary — it needs to be "the evidence of what happened." That's a fundamentally different bar. And it's exactly where several Claude Cowork limitations come into sharp focus. This article breaks down the seven critical gaps in Claude Cowork that make it a non-starter for core enterprise workflows — and what a purpose-built enterprise AI platform does differently. 1. No Audit Logs: Operating Inside a Compliance Black Box What it is: Claude Cowork does not generate immutable audit trails. According to Anthropic's own documentation and third-party security analyses, Cowork activity is excluded from Anthropic's audit logs, Compliance API, and data exports. There is no official, tamper-proof record of who accessed what, which workflow ran, or what decision was made. Why it matters for a bank or insurer: Regulators don't accept summaries. They want — as one compliance professional put it — "the exact moment a disclosure was made or missed. Not a summary. The actual citation." Without audit logs, you cannot prove process adherence during a regulatory examination, trace the origin of an error or breach, or satisfy internal audit requirements for KYC workflows, loan underwriting, or insurance claims. What Jinba does differently: Jinba Flow is built on comprehensive, immutable audit logging as a foundational requirement — not an add-on. Every workflow execution, every parameter change, and every decision is recorded and reviewable. This is core to Jinba's SOC II compliance posture and is what makes it viable for high-stakes processes like bank-to-bank KYC and investment document review where governance reporting isn't optional. 2. No RBAC or Team-Level Permissions: A Governance Nightmare What it is: Claude Cowork has no Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). It's architected for individuals, which means there's no mechanism to control who can build, view, edit, or trigger specific workflows — or who can access sensitive data within a workflow context. Why it matters for a bank or insurer: Without permissions governance, a junior analyst could theoretically trigger a workflow approving a multi-million dollar claim. A contractor could access customer PII. This directly undermines segregation of duties — a cornerstone requirement across virtually every financial regulation from SOX to GDPR. Enterprise practitioners are increasingly vocal about the "governance around AI-driven approvals" that their organizations need before they can deploy AI in operations. What Jinba does differently: Jinba is explicitly a team platform, not a personal productivity tool. It includes full RBAC, SSO, and Active Directory integration. Technical teams use Jinba Flow to build and version-control approved workflows. Non-technical business users then execute those workflows through Jinba App — with access restricted to only the workflows and data relevant to their role. Builders build. The team runs. Governance is enforced at every layer. 3. Not Suitable for Regulated Workloads — Per Anthropic's Own Documentation What it is: This isn't analyst opinion or competitive positioning — Anthropic's own documentation explicitly states that Claude Cowork is not designed or recommended for regulated workloads. The vendor itself warns against using it in compliance-heavy environments. Why it matters for a bank or insurer: Using a tool against its creator's explicit guidance is a significant legal and regulatory liability. If an issue surfaces during an audit or enforcement action, demonstrating due diligence becomes nearly impossible. In industries where compliance isn't optional, this is the clearest possible deal-breaker — and it applies regardless of how capable the underlying model is. What Jinba does differently: Jinba was built from the ground up for regulated environments. The platform is SOC II compliant and carries a proven track record across ~70 enterprise implementations , including MUFG/Mitsubishi Bank. When the vendor of your AI tool tells you not to use it for your core work, it's time to find a tool whose vendor says the opposite. 4. No On-Premise Deployment: A Data Residency Dead End What it is: Claude Cowork is a cloud-only product. There is no option to run it on-premise, in a private cloud, or in an air-gapped environment. Your data goes to Anthropic's infrastructure — full stop. Why it matters for a bank or insurer: Many large financial institutions, defense contractors, and healthcare organizations have strict data residency requirements that prohibit sensitive customer or proprietary data from leaving their own network perimeter. For these organizations, a cloud-only architecture isn't a feature tradeoff — it's a hard blocker. No on-premise option means no deployment. Full stop. What Jinba does differently: Jinba Flow and Jinba App both support on-premise and private cloud deployment, enabling enterprises to run powerful AI workflow automation inside their own infrastructure. Private model hosting is available via AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, or fully self-hosted models. For institutions operating in air-gapped environments — a reality for many Japanese megabanks and US federal credit unions — this flexibility isn't a nice-to-have. It's the baseline requirement that makes deployment possible at all. 5. Consumption Rate Unpredictability: The CFO's New Headache What it is: LLMs like Claude are stochastic by nature — meaning the same prompt can produce outputs of wildly different lengths and token counts. In Claude Cowork, this translates to variable, hard-to-predict costs per task. The same workflow executed 1,000 times won't cost the same each time. Why it matters for a bank or insurer: Enterprise AI spend jumped 108% year-over-year in 2026. CFOs are no longer treating AI infrastructure as a blank check — they're demanding ROI accountability and predictable cost structures. A core operational process with variable, effectively uncapped costs is a budgeting nightmare. It's also one of the primary reasons AI initiatives stall between pilot and production: you can't scale what you can't price. What Jinba does differently: Jinba's architecture directly solves the cost problem at a structural level. Its deterministic design — using 80% rule-based workflows — delivers consistent, auditable outputs with predictable costs. This approach generates a 15–60x cost advantage over stochastic AI agents, running at $5–20/month at scale versus $300+ for purely LLM-driven equivalents. For CFOs evaluating the AI budget line, Jinba's AI Consulting arm also offers an LLM Cost Audit to identify where token burn is happening and architect deterministic alternatives — turning an unpredictable R&D expense into a manageable operational line item. 6. Usage Limits Scale Per Individual, Not Per Team What it is: Claude Cowork's consumption limits and capabilities are tied to individual user accounts. There's no concept of pooled team capacity — meaning a 50-person KYC processing team doesn't get 50x the throughput. Each person is capped independently. Why it matters for a bank or insurer: Operations is a team sport. When individual usage caps create bottlenecks — only a handful of "power users" can run high-volume tasks — it creates inequitable resource distribution and forces workflows to be designed around tool limitations rather than business logic. This compounds the problem of Cowork being fundamentally an individual productivity tool rather than an enterprise operations layer. What Jinba does differently: Jinba's resource management operates at the team level. Workflows built in Jinba Flow become shared assets consumable by the entire team through Jinba App , governed by RBAC rather than individual seat limits. The model is explicitly team-first: builders build once, the whole team benefits, and permissions — not per-seat caps — determine who can do what. 7. No Cross-Session Memory: The Amnesiac Assistant What it is: Claude Cowork has no persistent memory across sessions. Every new conversation starts from a blank slate. Context, decisions, and prior interactions are lost the moment a session ends. Why it matters for a bank or insurer: Complex enterprise processes don't complete in a single chat session. Loan underwriting, insurance claims adjustment, and prior authorization workflows can span hours, days, or weeks — with multiple stakeholders contributing context at different stages. An AI assistant that resets after every session forces users to rebuild context from scratch, dramatically increasing the risk of error and the time to completion. For regulated audit workflows, this isn't just inefficient — it's a data integrity risk. What Jinba does differently: Jinba is designed for stateful, multi-session business processes. Workflows in Jinba Flow maintain context across executions, enabling long-running, multi-step processes to carry state forward without requiring manual re-entry of context. This is critical for any workflow where continuity directly impacts outcome quality — from underwriting decisions to multi-party contract reviews. Claude Cowork vs. Jinba: Side-by-Side Comparison Limitation Claude Cowork Jinba Audit Logs ❌ Excluded from Anthropic's Compliance API ✅ Comprehensive, immutable audit logging RBAC & Team Permissions ❌ Individual-only, no role governance ✅ Full RBAC, SSO, Active Directory integration Suitability for Regulated Workloads ❌ Advised against by Anthropic ✅ SOC II compliant, built for finance & healthcare On-Premise Deployment ❌ Cloud-only, no private/air-gapped option ✅ On-premise, private cloud, and self-hosted models Cost Predictability ❌ Stochastic token consumption, variable costs ✅ Deterministic architecture — 15–60x cost savings at scale Usage Limits ❌ Capped per individual account ✅ Team-level resource management via RBAC Cross-Session Memory ❌ Stateless — no context retained between sessions ✅ Stateful workflows with persistent cross-session memory The Right Tool for a High-Stakes Job Claude Cowork is a genuinely powerful AI assistant — for the individual on a laptop. But the seven Claude Cowork limitations outlined above aren't minor feature gaps. They are fundamental architectural choices that make it unsuitable for the serious, evidence-based, multi-stakeholder work of a regulated enterprise. No audit logs. No permissions. No on-premise option. Not recommended by its own creator for compliance workloads. These aren't workarounds waiting to be patched — they're the product. True enterprise AI requires a different foundation: one built on auditability, determinism, team governance, and deployment flexibility. That's not a nice-to-have in banking or insurance — it's the minimum bar for production deployment. If your organization is evaluating AI workflow automation and you're operating in a regulated environment, the question isn't whether Claude Cowork is impressive. It is. The question is whether it was built for your context. And the honest answer, per Anthropic's own docs, is no. Ready to see what purpose-built looks like? Jinba's team has worked through ~70 enterprise AI implementations in financial services — including MUFG/Mitsubishi Bank. We offer a free AI strategy assessment that gives your CIO a concrete roadmap for compliant, cost-effective AI automation. No vendor pitch — just a practical audit of where AI can move the needle in your environment, and what it will actually cost to get there. Get your free AI strategy assessment → Frequently Asked Questions Why is Claude Cowork not suitable for regulated industries like finance or healthcare? Claude Cowork is not suitable for regulated industries primarily because it lacks essential enterprise features like immutable audit logs, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and on-premise deployment options. These features are non-negotiable for compliance with regulations such as SOX, GDPR, and HIPAA. Anthropic's own documentation explicitly advises against using the tool for regulated workloads, creating a significant legal and compliance liability for any organization that does so. What are audit logs and why are they critical for enterprise AI? Audit logs are unchangeable, time-stamped records of all system activities, such as who accessed data, which workflows were run, and what decisions were made. For enterprises, especially in regulated sectors, these logs are critical for proving process adherence to auditors, tracing errors or security breaches, and satisfying internal governance requirements. Without them, it's impossible to provide the "evidence of what happened" that regulators demand. How does a deterministic AI model like Jinba's save costs compared to a stochastic one like Claude? A deterministic AI model saves costs by producing consistent, predictable outputs for the same inputs, which eliminates the variable token consumption inherent in stochastic LLMs like Claude. Jinba's architecture relies heavily on rule-based workflows, which are highly efficient and have predictable operational costs. This approach can be 15-60x more cost-effective at scale compared to purely LLM-driven tools, turning unpredictable AI spending into a manageable operational expense. What is Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and why does its absence in Claude Cowork matter? Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is a security system that restricts system access to authorized users based on their roles within an organization. Its absence in Claude Cowork means there is no way to control who can build, view, or execute specific workflows, or access sensitive data. This undermines the segregation of duties, a fundamental compliance principle, and creates significant risk, such as a junior employee accidentally triggering a high-stakes financial transaction. Can Claude Cowork be deployed on-premise or in a private cloud? No, Claude Cowork is a cloud-only product and cannot be deployed on-premise or in a private cloud environment. This is a critical limitation for many large enterprises in finance, defense, and healthcare that have strict data residency policies prohibiting sensitive data from leaving their own network perimeter. A cloud-only architecture is a hard blocker for these organizations. What is the main difference between an AI assistant like Claude Cowork and an enterprise AI platform like Jinba? The main difference is their core design purpose: Claude Cowork is a personal productivity tool for individuals, while Jinba is an enterprise AI platform built for team-based, regulated, and mission-critical workflows. This distinction is reflected in their features. Jinba is built with a foundation of auditability, team governance (RBAC), deployment flexibility (on-premise), and predictable costs, which are essential for enterprise operations but absent in individual-focused tools like Claude Cowork.

title: Best Wix Alternatives: Custom Design Without an Agency
summary: Six Wix alternatives compared on real year-one cost, export rights and design control. Every price read from the vendor's own page and dated.
body_text: How we checked these numbers Every price, limit and quota below was read off the vendor's own pricing page or help centre where those render to a fetch, and from dated independent write-ups cross-checked against each other where they do not. Webflow and Squarespace fall in that second group, because neither renders prices to a fetch. The load-bearing figures link to the page they came from. Wix, Squarespace, Webflow and WordPress figures were checked on 14 August 2026 ; Shopify, Hostinger and Blink on 18 August 2026 . Where a vendor's own pages contradict each other, we say so instead of picking the flattering one — that happened three times, and one of them was us. We have run no speed tests, Lighthouse audits or migration timings of our own, and none are invented here. Where a performance figure appears, it is someone else's published measurement, attributed to them. Most articles on this topic quote a "starting price" and stop. The numbers below are year-one totals including the add-ons that are not optional in practice. What Wix actually costs, and what it locks Wix's advertised entry price is not the price of a working business site. The published ladder runs Light $17/mo, Core $29/mo, Business $39/mo and Business Elite $159/mo billed annually. The free plan forces Wix ads and a wixsite.com subdomain, with no ecommerce and no analytics. Then the additions arrive. Custom business email is a separate ~$6/mo Google Workspace charge. App Market apps run $3–$20/mo each. The domain is free for year one, then renews around $13.35/yr. A native mobile app is a separate $99/mo Branded App plan , plus $99/yr to Apple and $25 one-time to Google. Twelve months in, the honest range is $204 bare minimum, about $540 for a typical small business on Core with email and one app, and $3,292 for a business on Business Elite that also wants the mobile app. That is arithmetic over Wix's own list prices. The structural limits matter more than the money: No export, no self-hosting. Content exports — products, contacts, orders, blog posts. The site does not. Worth knowing: Base44, which Wix owns , does offer real code export — ZIP download and GitHub integration — on paid plans. So this is a product decision, not a technical limit. No template switching. Rebuild from scratch to change the look. CMS ceilings force upgrades : 1,500 items on Light, 4,000 on Core, 20,000 on Business , with dedicated database infrastructure only at Business Elite. Wix Harmony runs on credits. Wix's AI builder, launched 21 January 2026, is metered — Core reportedly carries 500 AI credits a month. Run out and you wait for the next cycle or buy a top-up. Give Wix its due on two real things. It charges 0% platform transaction fees on every plan across 20+ payment gateways, better than several rivals. And ease of use is its best-evidenced strength: Capterra's Ease of Use sub-score is 4.5 out of 5 across 10,702 reviewers , its highest of four sub-scores. Neither is why you are leaving. You are leaving because you cannot make it look like you, and you cannot take it with you. 1. Blink — the site is designed for you, and it stays yours Blink's template gallery: 42+ production builds including a plant boutique, a luxury dental clinic and an architecture studio — starting points, not the only path Blink Price: Free (5 build credits a day, capped at 30/month, preview URLs only) · Starter $25/mo · Pro $50/mo · Max from $200/mo · Team, per seat with a shared credit pool. Annual billing is offered — check the current discount on the pricing page, because Blink's own pages disagree on it. Best for: the owner, or the agency, who wants a studio-quality site built to a brief and edited by describing changes Blink does not hand you a catalogue. You describe the business, and the site is designed and built for it — layout, copy, imagery, structure — then hosted on your own custom domain with SSL issued and renewed automatically across CloudFront's edge network. One product, one bill, nothing to wire together. Design that is not a template. The 42+ starting points are production builds, and they are optional. The default path is a site designed to your description, which is why it does not carry the visual signature every template platform has. Changes are a sentence. This is what ends the agency dependency. Point at an element in the visual editor, say what is wrong, batch your feedback to the AI. No drag handles, no ticket, no waiting for someone to have a free hour. Build and host in one place. A per-project managed SQL database with row-level security on by default, built-in authentication across Google, GitHub, Apple, Microsoft, email and magic links, file storage and deployment — included in the plan rather than bought separately. Hosting is metered in plan credits from 50 a month at the 10,000-visit tier, and Blink states plainly that traffic overages never take your app offline . The economics, for the agency. There is no per-site plan and no per-seat wall around your client: Team workspaces pool credits across every seat and make viewer seats unlimited and free , so stakeholders and clients cost nothing to include. What you delete is the per-client stack — no theme licence, no page-builder licence, no caching plugin, no security plugin, no separate hosting account, and no unpaid support hours after handover, because the client edits the site by describing the change. That is the margin difference: you bill the same project fee and stop buying the cost side of it. SEO and AI search are a panel, not a project. Blink's SEO & AI Search panel, shipped 15 June 2026, scans your live site, scores it 0–100 across five levers, and applies fixes in one click. Page titles, meta descriptions, sitemap, robots.txt, JSON-LD structured data and Open Graph images are controlled in-product, with guidance for publishing an /llms.txt so AI search engines can read you. And unlike the platform you are leaving, the exit is written down. Blink's terms state you "retain full ownership of any code, applications, or other content" you create and may "use, modify, distribute, publish, sell, or open-source" it. Concretely: a code download, two-way GitHub sync that also pulls back edits made in VS Code or Cursor, and a documented self-host route with a Dockerfile template naming Vercel, Netlify, Railway and Render. The honest limitations: the free tier is a preview, not a live site — production hosting, a custom domain, code download and badge removal all start at Starter, $25/mo — and free-plan projects are public by default. Starter and Pro plan credits reset each cycle and do not roll over; only Max credits carry forward, though purchased credit packs never expire. Hosting traffic draws on the same credit pool as building, so a busy month costs credits you would otherwise spend on changes. And all fees are non-refundable, including partially used billing periods. Verdict: if you want a professional site that is genuinely yours, that you can change the same afternoon you decide to, hosted and SEO-ready without a second vendor — this is the one. Start free at blink.new . Already have a Wix site whose content you like? Type /clone-url followed by your current URL and Blink rebuilds it as a starting point, so you edit rather than start from a blank page. Full breakdown: Blink vs Wix . 2. Squarespace — the best template catalogue, and you are renting the design Squarespace's homepage, leading with template-driven design and a 14-day trial — there is no permanent free plan Blink Price: Basic $19/mo · Core $29/mo · Plus $49/mo · Advanced $99/mo, all billed annually. No free plan — a 14-day trial only. Best for: a portfolio, restaurant or boutique brand that wants to look excellent immediately and will not restructure later Nobody has a better catalogue of pre-made templates. Roughly 200 designer-made options let someone with no design skill ship something professional on day one, and Capterra rates it 4.6 out of 5 across 3,415 reviews . Tooltester measured 99.96% uptime in its own monitoring. That is a different thing from a site designed around your business. The ceiling on a Squarespace site is how close your business happens to sit to one of those 200 templates, and the same opinionated system that makes it look good is the wall you meet: rigid page layouts, block-sizing constraints, only one navigation level below the main menu — and on version 7.1 you cannot switch templates after launch . The export is the harder problem. Squarespace's documentation is explicit that the export is a partial, one-way WordPress-oriented XML file carrying layout pages, one blog page and its posts, and text and image blocks. It does not carry style settings, custom CSS, store pages, portfolio pages, event pages, index pages, or any blog page beyond the first. Squarespace also states you cannot export from one Squarespace site and import into another. Costs moved recently, and against customers. On 17 July 2026 Squarespace raised prices by up to 26% — annual Core from $23 to $29, Plus from $39 to $49 — notified by email with no public memo, as reported by PetaPixel . Scheduling (Acuity, $16–$49/mo), Member Areas ($9–$35/mo) and Email Campaigns (from $8/mo) are separate subscriptions, not plan features. Two limits matter if organic traffic pays your bills: you cannot edit robots.txt or the sitemap, and Tooltester measured Squarespace's mobile page-speed score at 28.94 — last among the twelve builders they tested. Verdict: the right pick if your site is a beautiful brochure that will not change much and you accept you are renting the design. If the site must evolve with the business, you will meet the frame. See Blink vs Squarespace . 3. Webflow — control you operate yourself, priced per axis Webflow's homepage, positioning itself as a website experience platform for design and marketing teams rather than solo owners Blink Price: Site Basic $15/mo · Site Premium $25/mo · Workspace Core $19/mo (required for code export) · each additional Full Seat $39/mo — all billed annually Best for: an in-house design team, or an agency with a dedicated Webflow specialist Webflow gives you the most direct control of any visual tool here — box model, flexbox, breakpoints and z-index, exposed. That is a skill purchase, not a design outcome. WebsiteBuilderExpert scored its design capability 4.6/5 and its ease of use 2.1 out of 5 — the lowest of any builder they tested — and explicitly redirects beginners elsewhere. The pricing catches business owners because it bills on three axes at once. Site plans are per website . Workspace plans are separate, and code export requires at least Core at $19/mo. Seats are separate again: one Full Seat included, the next at $39/mo. Basic, at $15/mo, has no CMS at all , so any site with a blog starts at Premium. A realistic year one is $540 at the low end (Premium site + Core workspace + domain), about $1,020 typical with a second editor and one gap-filler tool, and $3,876 for a small team with extra seats, bandwidth and third-party tooling. If you are an agency, run the multiplication before you commit. Ten client sites for a year is 10 × Premium ($300/yr each) = $3,000 , plus a Core workspace at $228/yr, plus one extra Full Seat at $468/yr — $3,696 before a single hour of work , and every new client adds another $300. Two 2026 changes matter before you commit. The May 2026 restructure cut included bandwidth on the Business path from 100 GB to 50 GB , and two consecutive overage months automatically upgrade your plan. And Webflow discontinued its native User Accounts (memberships) feature on 29 January 2026 , after disabling its Logic automation product in June 2025 — gated content now needs a third-party service such as Memberstack, around $25/mo. The export is narrower than buyers assume: static HTML, CSS, JS and assets, but no working CMS content, forms, site search, ecommerce or memberships. Collection lists render empty; forms submit nowhere. It is a design artifact, not a running site. Verdict: right when a designer owns the site as their job. For an owner who wants the outcome rather than the craft, the curve and the three-axis bill are the whole story. 4. WordPress — maximum ownership, maximum maintenance WordPress.com's homepage — the managed face of the open-source software that still runs roughly 41.9% of the web Blink Price: WordPress.com Personal $4/mo · Premium $8/mo · Business $25/mo · Commerce $45/mo, billed annually. Self-hosted WordPress.org is free software plus your own hosting and domain. Best for: someone with a developer, who wants nobody to be able to lock them out, ever On one axis WordPress is unbeatable, and it is worth saying plainly: because the software is GPLv2 and you can self-host it, no vendor can hold your site hostage. You own the files and the database outright. That is why it still runs roughly 41.9% of all websites. The cost of that ownership is that you become the operations team. The security surface is the clearest number. Patchstack recorded 11,334 new vulnerabilities across the WordPress ecosystem in 2025, up 42% year over year — 91% in plugins, 17% rated high severity, and 46% publicly disclosed while still unpatched. Capterra's review-topic tallies agree: 1,255 reviews mention bugs and plugin conflicts (74% negative), 1,222 mention security (75% negative), 765 mention speed (77% negative). Pricing is less simple than the sticker, too. Self-hosted looks cheap until renewal: Bluehost's Basic promo runs $2.95/mo and renews near $9.99/mo; SiteGround's StartUp goes from $2.99 to $17.99/mo. The standard plugin stack recurs annually — Elementor Pro $59/yr, WP Rocket $59/yr, Wordfence Premium $149/yr, with Wordfence's free tier withholding new threat signatures for around 30 days. A realistic first year is $51 bare-bones, $229 typical, $462 at renewal rates with a security plugin. Credit where due: Automattic opened plugin installation to every paid plan on 2 April 2026 , including the $4/mo Personal tier, removing a long-standing $252/yr jump. Verdict: correct if ownership beats everything and you have — or are — a developer. If your actual goal is a site that looks good and changes easily, you are buying a maintenance job to get there. 5. Shopify — the right answer when the catalogue is the business Shopify's homepage, built around commerce infrastructure — checkout, POS and fulfilment rather than general-purpose site design Blink Price: Basic $29/mo · Grow $79/mo · Advanced $299/mo billed yearly ($39/$105/$399 monthly) · Plus from $2,300/mo. No free plan — a 3-day trial, then $1/month for three months. Best for: a real product catalogue with inventory, fulfilment and in-person sales If you are leaving Wix because the store outgrew it, Shopify is the honest answer and we are not going to pretend otherwise. Card rates step down as you climb — 2.9% + 30¢ on Basic, 2.7% on Grow, 2.5% on Advanced, 2.25% on Plus — and third-party gateway fees fall from 2% to 1% to 0.6% to 0.2%. Bandwidth is unlimited on every plan with no overage fees, and SSL is free on any domain you add. Two things to price in properly. No domain is bundled — domains start around $9/yr, and Shopify states outright that "renewal pricing may differ from initial purchase and can change over time," with the renewal figure shown only in-admin. And annual billing is effectively mandatory to hit the advertised numbers: $39/$105/$399 monthly against $29/$79/$299 yearly is about a third more. The portability picture is mixed. Theme code is genuinely editable, with GitHub integration, a CLI and a VS Code extension. But a Shopify theme is Liquid, which needs a Shopify backend to render — the theme is not a site you can host elsewhere, and your products, orders, customers and checkout do not live in it. Verdict: if the catalogue is the business, use Shopify. If the store is one section of a site whose job is to explain, rank and convert, you are buying a commerce platform to solve a website problem. 6. Hostinger — the cheapest sticker, once you read the billing Hostinger's website builder page, leading with a $2.99/mo headline that requires a 48-month upfront commitment Blink Price: Premium $2.99/mo · Unlimited $3.99/mo · Cloud Startup $7.99/mo — all promotional. No free plan; 14-day trial and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Best for: the lowest possible outlay on a simple site, if you are willing to prepay for four years Hostinger genuinely is the cheapest entry on this page, and it bundles a custom domain free for the first year. It is also the entry where the headline number needs the most translation. That $2.99/mo is not a monthly price. Hostinger states plainly: "All plans are paid upfront. The monthly rate reflects the total plan price divided by the number of months in your plan." The $2.99 rate is $143.52 charged upfront for 48 months, and it renews at $10.99/mo — $131.88/yr thereafter. Unlimited renews at $203.88/yr, Cloud Startup at $311.88/yr. Prices are listed excluding VAT. The bundled .com renews at $19.99/yr after its $0.01 first year, and the free-domain offer excludes monthly plans, upgrades and renewals. The AI product, Hostinger Horizons, is metered twice over: "AI credits for website and app creation" (5 on Premium, 15 on Unlimited) and a separate pool of "credits for AI agents" (none on Premium, 500 on Unlimited, 1000 on Cloud Startup). Reverting with Undo does not refund consumed credits. Export deserves a flag. Horizons does offer a code export, but it is one-way — Hostinger states "there is no way to import the edited version back to Horizons and continue with prompting." Hostinger's own documentation also contradicts itself on the format, with the export article describing a Node.js/React/Vite project and the technical-specifications article describing a static website. Both were current when we checked on 18 August 2026. Verdict: genuinely the cheapest way to put something simple online, provided you understand you are prepaying four years and that the AI path is one-way. It is a hosting company that added a builder, and it prices like one. Side by side Blink Wix Squarespace Webflow WordPress Shopify Hostinger Entry price, live site $25/mo $17/mo $19/mo $15/mo (no CMS) $4/mo (.com) $29/mo $2.99/mo* Realistic year one $300–$2,400 $204–$3,292 $228–$2,196 $540–$3,876 $51–$462 $348+ $35.88 (of $143.52 prepaid) Renews at Same Same Same Same 4–6× on hosting Same $131.88/yr Free tier publishes live? Preview URL only Yes, with ads None webflow.io only Yes, with ads None None Site built to your brief Yes, from a prompt Template + credits Template You build it You or a developer Template + AI Template + credits Change it by describing it Yes Partly (credits) No No No Partly Partly (credits) Get your code out Download, GitHub sync, Docker self-host (Starter+) None at all Partial, lossy XML Static only; CMS/forms/ecom break Full — you own it Theme only; needs Liquid backend One-way only Switch design later Yes, describe it No — rebuild No on 7.1 Yes, you rebuild it Yes, swap theme Yes, swap theme Yes, swap template Database + auth included Yes CMS, item caps No Only via Webflow Cloud; auth removed Jan 2026 Via plugins Commerce only No Per-site / per-seat billing Neither; viewers free Per site Per site Per site AND per seat Per site Per store Per plan Domain included Connect your own Free year 1 Free year 1 No Free year 1 (.com) No, ~$9/yr Free year 1 Robots.txt / sitemap control Yes Yes No Yes Yes Yes, via Liquid Sitemap auto *Hostinger's $2.99/mo requires $143.52 paid upfront for 48 months. Every other figure is a genuine monthly or annual rate. Wix, Squarespace, Webflow and WordPress checked 14 August 2026; Shopify, Hostinger and Blink 18 August 2026. Moving off Wix without rebuilding it by hand You cannot export a Wix site, so you rebuild — but you do not rebuild by hand. Wix gives you no site export, and that means no tool can properly "import" a Wix site. What it does give you is a live, public URL, and that is enough. In Blink, type /clone-url followed by your Wix address. Blink reads the live site and rebuilds it as a starting point, so you begin by editing a version of your own site instead of staring at a blank prompt. From there you describe what you always wanted it to be. Then the mechanical parts, in order: export your Wix data — products, contacts, orders, blog posts as XML — since that is what Wix does let you take · rebuild and review on the preview URL · point your domain by CNAME to cname.blink.new , with SSL issued automatically within 5–10 minutes of DNS verification · keep URL paths matching the old ones wherever they were earning traffic, and redirect the ones that changed · then cancel Wix. One timing note that costs people money: Wix subscriptions auto-renew, and billing is the most consistent hard complaint in the public record — the Better Business Bureau lists 920 complaints over three years, 416 closed in the last twelve months, with documented disputes of $324, $1,116 and £360. The honest counterweight is that BBB still accredits Wix and rates it A+, so this is a friction pattern rather than a scandal. Check the renewal date before you start, and cancel deliberately. Pick by who you are You are a business owner who outgrew the template. Use Blink . You get a site designed for your business rather than chosen from a grid, hosted on your domain with SSL, with an SEO panel that scores and fixes the live site — and you change it by describing the change, without booking anyone's time. You are escaping the lock-in. Use Blink . WordPress gives you the same files and the job of running them forever — ownership you have to operate. Blink gives you the files and someone else operating them, and you can still walk with the code any day you want: download, GitHub sync, or a documented Docker self-host path. You are an agency shipping client sites. Use Blink . There is no per-site plan and no per-seat charge for the client — Webflow's equivalent is $3,696 a year before you do any work, and it grows $300 with every new client. You delete the theme licence, the builder licence, the security plugin and the separate hosting account, and you hand over a site the client edits by typing a sentence, which is how the project ends instead of becoming support. And the cases where we would send you elsewhere: one gorgeous portfolio you will never restructure, go to Squarespace. A designer on staff whose job is the website, go to Webflow. A real product catalogue with inventory and fulfilment, go to Shopify. Total ownership with a developer to run it, go to self-hosted WordPress. Those are good answers to different questions. If your question was the one at the top of this page, the answer is Blink. Frequently asked questions No. Wix's own help centre states a Wix site must be hosted and operated on Wix's servers, and there is no full-site or source-code export on the classic Editor or on Wix Studio. You can export content — products, contacts, orders, invoices and blog posts as XML — but not the site itself. In practice you rebuild elsewhere, which is why Blink's /clone-url command exists: it reads your live Wix URL and rebuilds it as a starting point, so you are editing rather than starting over. Hostinger has the lowest sticker at $2.99/mo, but that is $143.52 paid upfront for 48 months and it renews at $131.88/yr. Self-hosted WordPress is about $51 for a bare-bones first year if you supply the labour, then rises as promotional hosting renews — Bluehost from $2.95 to about $9.99/mo, SiteGround from $2.99 to $17.99/mo — and the standard plugin stack recurs annually. Blink's Starter plan at $25/mo includes hosting, SSL, a custom domain, a database and the AI that does the work, which is the comparison that matters if your time has a price. No. Wix documents that once a site is built and published on a template, changing template means rebuilding from scratch on a new site, reusing only the domain and manually re-entered content. Squarespace 7.1 carries the same restriction after launch. This is the limitation that makes template platforms feel like a trap three years in, and it is the reason a prompt-driven builder behaves differently: in Blink you change the design by describing the change, not by starting a new site. Judge it on the controls the platform actually gives you. Squarespace is weakest: you cannot edit robots.txt or the sitemap, cannot exclude pages or set priority, and canonical tags and advanced schema are not directly controllable. Wix, Webflow, WordPress, Shopify and Blink all give you editable robots.txt, sitemaps, redirects and structured data. Blink adds an SEO & AI Search panel that scans the live site, scores it 0–100 across five levers and applies fixes in one click, plus guidance on publishing an /llms.txt file so AI search engines can read your site. Only for WordPress and Webflow in practice. WebsiteBuilderExpert scored Webflow 2.1/5 on ease of use — the lowest of any builder they tested — because it exposes the CSS box model, flexbox and breakpoints directly. Self-hosted WordPress makes you responsible for updates, plugin conflicts and security patching. Squarespace, Wix, Shopify and Hostinger need no code but limit you to what the template allows. Blink needs no code at all: you describe what you want in plain English and refine it by pointing at an element and saying what is wrong. Wix and WordPress.com have permanent free tiers. Squarespace, Shopify and Hostinger have none — only trials of 14 days, 3 days and 14 days respectively. But read what "free" gates: Wix Free forces Wix ads and a wixsite.com subdomain with no ecommerce, and WordPress.com Free shows ads you cannot remove and blocks plugin installation. Blink's free tier gives you 5 build credits a day, capped at 30 a month, on a preview URL with a database and authentication included; publishing to your own domain starts at Starter, $25/mo. Between $204 and $3,292 depending on what you need, against an advertised entry of $17/mo. The low end is the Light plan alone. A typical small business on Core with custom email and one App Market app lands near $540. The high end is Business Elite at $1,908/yr plus the separate $99/mo Branded App plan and the Apple ($99/yr) and Google ($25) developer accounts. Custom email is not bundled, App Market apps run $3–$20/mo each, and the free first-year domain renews at about $13.35/yr. Blink, for two reasons an agency feels immediately. First, the billing shape: there is no per-site plan and no charge for giving a client access, where ten Webflow client sites cost $3,696 a year before any work and grow $300 per new client. Second, what you hand over: on Wix, Squarespace or Webflow the client returns to you for every change, which is either unpaid support or a retainer you have to sell. With Blink the client edits by describing the change, so the handover is final. Webflow remains the stronger choice if you employ a full-time Webflow specialist and sell design craft as the deliverable.

body_text: New research suggests some blood-thinning drugs may be linked to slower cognitive decline in people with atrial fibrillation and Alzheimer’s. Here is what the findings mean. Could blood-thinning drugs slow Alzheimer’s disease? A new study has raised an intriguing possibility in the search for ways to slow the progression of Alzheimer’s disease. Researchers have found that certain modern blood-thinning medications may be associated with a slower decline in cognitive function among people who have both atrial fibrillation and Alzheimer’s. The findings are particularly interesting because anticoagulant medicines are already widely prescribed for people with atrial fibrillation, a common heart rhythm condition that can increase the risk of blood clots and stroke. However, the research does not mean that people should start taking blood thinners to prevent or treat Alzheimer’s disease. The researchers say further investigation is needed before these medicines could be considered specifically for their potential effects on dementia. What did the new Alzheimer’s study find? Researchers from Sweden examined health information from more than 7,000 people diagnosed with both atrial fibrillation and Alzheimer’s disease. The participants were grouped according to whether they were taking newer anticoagulant medicines, the older blood thinner warfarin, or no anticoagulant treatment. The researchers then assessed cognitive performance, including areas such as memory, language and motor skills. The results suggested that people taking newer anticoagulants experienced a somewhat slower decline in cognitive function than people taking warfarin or those who were not receiving anticoagulant treatment. The difference was relatively small over a single year. People taking newer blood thinners scored just under 1 per cent higher on the cognitive assessment after one year. Although that may appear modest, researchers say even small differences could potentially become more meaningful over longer periods. Why could blood thinners affect the brain? The possible explanation centres on the relationship between the heart, blood vessels and the brain. Atrial fibrillation can interfere with the heart's normal rhythm and increase the likelihood of blood clots. Those clots can travel to the brain and cause a stroke. Even very small disruptions to blood flow may potentially contribute to damage in the brain over time. Researchers believe that anticoagulant treatment could potentially protect brain health indirectly by reducing clot formation and helping to prevent vascular events. The idea is particularly relevant because Alzheimer's disease does not occur in isolation from other health conditions. Changes affecting blood vessels and circulation can also contribute to cognitive problems. According to the researchers, improving blood flow and reducing small-scale vascular damage could potentially have a positive effect on cognition. Importantly, this remains an area of scientific investigation rather than an established treatment for Alzheimer's. Newer anticoagulants appeared to perform differently One of the most notable aspects of the research was the difference between newer anticoagulants and warfarin. Newer medications, sometimes referred to as direct oral anticoagulants, include drugs such as rivaroxaban. These medicines are increasingly used instead of warfarin for many people with atrial fibrillation. The study associated newer anticoagulants with slower cognitive decline compared with both warfarin and no anticoagulant treatment. The researchers also observed that people receiving newer anticoagulants had lower rates of some serious outcomes, including stroke and premature death, compared with people who were not receiving anticoagulant therapy. Warfarin was also associated with lower risks of certain outcomes compared with receiving no anticoagulant treatment, although it was linked with a greater risk of major bleeding. These findings highlight why anticoagulant treatment needs to be carefully tailored to each individual. Does this mean blood thinners could prevent Alzheimer’s? Not at this stage. The study was observational, meaning researchers examined existing health data rather than assigning participants randomly to different treatments. This type of research can identify associations, but it cannot prove that a medication directly caused the slower cognitive decline. There may also be other differences between people taking different medicines that influence the results. For this reason, researchers have stopped short of recommending anticoagulants as an Alzheimer's treatment for people who do not otherwise need them. Blood thinners can have serious side effects, particularly bleeding. Taking an anticoagulant without a medical reason could therefore create significant risks. Anyone already taking an anticoagulant should not stop or change their medication based on this study. Medication decisions should always be discussed with a doctor or qualified healthcare professional. The connection between atrial fibrillation and dementia The research also draws attention to the relationship between heart health and brain health. Atrial fibrillation becomes more common with age and is associated with an increased risk of stroke. Several cardiovascular risk factors, including high blood pressure, obesity and smoking, can also affect long-term brain health. This means looking after cardiovascular health may be an important part of protecting cognitive health as people get older. Maintaining healthy blood pressure, avoiding smoking, staying physically active, eating a balanced diet and managing conditions such as diabetes can all form part of a broader approach to reducing dementia risk. However, no single lifestyle change can guarantee that someone will avoid Alzheimer's disease. What should people take from the research? The most important message is that the study provides another potential avenue for Alzheimer's research, rather than a new treatment recommendation. The findings suggest that medicines already used to manage cardiovascular conditions may have effects on brain health that scientists do not yet fully understand. Future clinical trials will be important to determine whether newer anticoagulants genuinely slow cognitive decline and, if so, which patients could potentially benefit. Until then, people should continue taking prescribed medicines as directed and speak to their healthcare professional before making changes. The research also reinforces a broader lesson: heart and brain health are closely connected. Managing cardiovascular risk factors may be an important part of maintaining cognitive health throughout later life. Final thoughts Alzheimer’s disease remains one of the major health challenges associated with ageing, and researchers continue to investigate treatments that could slow its progression. The latest Swedish research offers an interesting clue. Among people with atrial fibrillation and Alzheimer's, newer blood-thinning medicines were associated with a slightly slower decline in cognitive function. But an association is not proof of cause and effect. More research is needed before anticoagulants could be considered specifically as a strategy for treating or preventing Alzheimer's disease. For now, the findings should be viewed as promising research rather than medical advice. People with atrial fibrillation should discuss their individual treatment options with their doctor, particularly because anticoagulants can reduce the risk of dangerous blood clots but can also increase the risk of bleeding. title: SentinelOne Makes the Autonomous SOC Trustworthy with Governed, Closed-Loop Response
summary: Purple AI and Singularity Hyperautomation now autonomously investigate alerts, reach verdicts, and execute responses inside boundaries set by human security teams
body_text: Purple AI and Singularity Hyperautomation now autonomously investigate alerts, reach verdicts, and execute responses inside boundaries set by human security teams LAS VEGAS, Nevada – August 3, 2026 – SentinelOne® (NYSE: S), the AI Security leader, today announced governed, closed-loop response across the Singularity™ Platform, delivering trustworthy automation for security operations. Purple AI® and Singularity Hyperautomation now autonomously investigate alerts, reach verdicts, and execute responses. Security teams set the boundaries first, deciding where AI acts on its own and where it stops for human sign-off. The Autonomous SOC now runs from alert to action, at the speed and scale of AI, with the confidence and control of human defenders. SOC teams have tried to embrace automation for years to deal with an overwhelming volume of alerts and data. Response automation was first attempted through SOAR playbooks, though those playbooks are fixed decision trees that break the moment reality diverges from the script. What stayed missing was judgment at the point of action. Purple AI supplies it, choosing the next step from what the investigation actually found rather than from a branch encoded months earlier. The loop closes. The foundation is already carrying a production load. Purple AI Agentic Investigation has been running in customer environments since June, and now handles more than 8,500 critical autonomous investigations every day. More than a third of the eligible customer base has it running. Across that base, Purple AI investigates nearly three times as many alerts as analysts reach by hand. Alerts that would have aged in a queue get investigated, and analysts spend their hours on the decisions that need judgment. “ Security teams need AI they can trust to act within boundaries they set, ” said Chris Corde, Chief Product Officer, SentinelOne. “ With this release, teams decide exactly where Purple AI is permitted to execute autonomously, and where it pauses for a human. That governance is what makes autonomous response viable in a live SOC. Human response time stretches on nights and weekends – attack timelines do not. In a single recent weekend, Purple AI investigated more than 5,000 critical alerts across our customer base, each in minutes. Nothing waited for Monday. ” What decides whether a SOC can adopt autonomous response based on agentic reasoning is whether a human can see the action, trace it, and take it back. Every AI-driven action in the Singularity Platform is traceable, auditable, and overrideable by the team that authorized it. Not every workflow needs to run unattended. The discipline is relevant control, staying in the decisions that carry real consequence and letting the rest run. Governance is the precondition, not the paperwork. These capabilities are built into core components of the Singularity Platform. SOC teams get AI reasoning and automated execution inside the workflows, tools, and approval chains they already run. There is no integration work and no additional tooling required. Building on Purple AI Agentic Investigation, the new capabilities use Singularity Hyperautomation workflows to: Trigger a Purple AI Agentic Investigation from any point in a workflow, not only the initial alert. Pull the full investigation report, with verdict and evidence, directly into automation logic. Apply customizable LLM Actions to reason over the findings and call the right next step. Call validated response snippets, reusable action blocks teams build once and use repeatedly. The Hyperautomation workflow capabilities are expected to be generally available later this quarter. SentinelOne is demonstrating them at Black Hat USA 2026 in booth #2933, and a full demo is available on the SentinelOne YouTube channel . Built for those who secure our world, its platform delivers unified coverage across endpoints, identity, cloud, and AI. Powered by Autonomous Security Intelligence, SentinelOne stops attacks at machine speed, reducing risk and delivering clarity and control to stay one step ahead. Headquartered in Mountain View, California with teams worldwide, SentinelOne protects nearly one-fifth of the Fortune 500 and hundreds of Global 2000 enterprises. From Main Street to Wall Street, the world’s most critical organizations trust SentinelOne with their security. Media Contact: Regan DePinto [email protected]
